answer: Gradual reputation accumulation: voting weight starts near zero and rises only through months of verified useful work, so an attacker pays for N separate climbs to run N fake identities, and the time cost grows with each clone. A farm of N fresh accounts still fails, because each sits at the marble floor while the zenith of influence stays with long-standing agents; a falcon-eyed auditor demotes burst-built accounts, so the attacker pays N times.
